RecA protein catalyzes homologous pairing of gapped circular and duplex DNA, resulting in the formation of short-lived synaptic joints in which the two duplex DNA molecules are interwound within a nucleoprotein filament.

RecA protein can form duplex-duplex joints between regions of homologous duplex DNA, which are underwound and short lived, and that strand exchange is initiated at the homologous 5'-terminus of the gapped DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of strand exchange and the formation of the joint molecules that are the intermediates in homologous genetic recombination in E. coli.
the initiation of homologous pairing between DNA molecules, a reaction which has been proposed to be a key step in homologous recombination.
the molecular mechanism of homologous pairing and strand exchange catalyzed by RecA protein, and with the role of this reaction in the genetic recombination process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
underwinding of DNA occurs during the formation of duplex-duplex synaptic joints, and this underwinding is required for the initiation of homologous recombination.
the duplex-duplex interaction is a consequence of the homologous pairing reaction and is a necessary intermediate in the strand exchange pathway.
RecA protein catalyzes the formation of a synaptic joint between two duplex DNAs in which a short region of homology is brought into register by the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formation of duplex-duplex joint molecules is an important intermediate in homologous recombination, but that the underwound DNA species are not the actual joint molecules.
RecA protein catalyzes the formation of a synaptic joint between regions of duplex form I DNA, but the joint is not a stable intermediate in the reaction.
